claims.text: In the BEA '2020 Personal Income and Outlays — Historical Comparisons' table, under the 'Current dollars' section, annual PCE in 2020 declined from the preceding year by $399.3 billion (dollar change), or -2.7 percent.

claims.text: The two PCE series do not use the same basis: the first is in current dollars (nominal) and the second is in chained dollars (inflation-adjusted, real), as indicated by the separate section headings 'Current dollars' and 'Chained dollars' in the 2020 annual comparisons table.

claims.text: A reader might conflate this annual table with the monthly (February 2021) table in the same document, which shows a PCE monthly dollar change of -149.0 billion current dollars and -162.7 billion chained dollars; those figures refer to the change from the preceding month (February 2021), not the annual 2020 change.

claims.text: One might question whether -2.7% (current dollars) vs -3.9% (chained dollars) is consistent; it is, because the chained-dollar decline exceeds the nominal decline when prices rose (PCE price index +1.2 percent from the preceding year), but the source does not explicitly reconcile the two series.
